result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): docs/issues/ISS-0766.yaml read in full. Its root cause is DIFFERENT in mechanism from this issue, though the same general class (shared/non-partitioned test-DB state under parallel load): ISS-0766 is test/support/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex's on_exit restoration of one FIXED row (the bpm-default tenant) racing another test's setup; it remains status: open (not resolved), with escalating reproduction-rate notes through 2026-09-24. ISS-0829/ISS-0825 is NOT a recurrence of ISS-0766's specific root cause -- it is a distinct mechanism in a different module, so no severity escalation on that basis, but both are instances of 'this suite's shared, per-partition Postgres database lets an unrelated concurrently-running test's activity leak into a test that assumes a closed/fixed data set.'

STEP 1 (diagnose): Read test/letflow/platform/migration_rollout_test.exs's EO-004 (lines 334-393) and EO-005 (lines 399-437) bodies directly, then traced the production code they call in lib/letflow/platform/migration_rollout.ex and its design doc.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by direct code trace + the design doc's own explicitly-flagged open question, not speculation): Letflow.Platform.MigrationRollout's repeat-call path (`apply_to_existing_rollout/2`, migration_rollout.ex:218-256, reached by start_rollout/3's second call in EO-005) re-evaluates `active_company_tenant_ids/0` (migration_rollout.ex:423-432 -- every tenant with `status == :active` AND a Registration row, scoped to the WHOLE shared per-partition database, not to any set of tenants a caller created) on every call, and sweeps any newly-active tenant it finds into the rollout's scope by registering + seeding a brand-new outcome row for it (lines 230-243, comment: 'A company that became active/provisioned after this rollout first started -- register + apply for it now, extending the rollout's scope'). This is confirmed as an intentional, explicitly-flagged production design choice, not a bug: lib/letflow/design/req374-tenant-migration-fanout-runner.md section 9, OQ-1 ('scope drift on a repeat start_rollout/3 call') says verbatim: '...it means a \"zero writes\" re-run (EO-005) is only literally zero-write when *no new company became eligible* since the rollout completed -- which is true in this requirement's own test scenario (a fixed company set) but may not hold in general platform operation.'

EO-005 assumes exactly the 'fixed company set' precondition OQ-1 names as fragile: it asserts GLOBAL `Repo.aggregate(Rollout/Outcome, :count, :id)` equality and `Enum.all?(second_result.outcomes, & &1.already_current)` between its two back-to-back start_rollout/3 calls. Under `scripts/test_parallel.sh -N 4`, each partition gets its own Postgres database (config/test.exs:65, `database: \"letflow_test#{MIX_TEST_PARTITION}\"`) but WITHIN one partition, 110+ other DataCase test files call `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` (grep-confirmed) and run `async: true` (the suite default) concurrently with this file's `async: false` tests in that SAME per-partition database. If any of those unrelated tests activates+provisions a tenant in the narrow window between EO-005's two start_rollout calls (or, for EO-004, in the window that lands a leaked tenant whose own real DDL never resolves to \"succeeded\" before EO-004's final `resumed_result.rollout.status == \"completed\"` assertion, since resume_rollout/apply_outstanding only ever mark the rollout \"completed\" once every one of its outcome rows, including any newly swept-in one, is \"succeeded\" -- recompute_rollout_completion), the exact-equality/all-succeeded assertions in EO-004/EO-005 break. Grep confirms no other test file calls MigrationRollout.start_rollout/resume_rollout, so this is not cross-file Rollout/Outcome-row contamination -- it is tenant-scope leakage via active_company_tenant_ids/0's global, unscoped active-tenant scan.

The SAME file already carries a proven fix pattern for this exact hazard class in its adjacent 'queryable outcome record' describe block (lines 288-327), whose own comment cites ISS-0716 and defends by asserting `length(result.outcomes) >= 2` (not `==`) and filtering strictly by tenant_id via `outcome_for/2`, rather than a global count or an all()-style predicate. EO-004/EO-005 were written without that same defensive scoping even though the design doc flagged the risk at design time (OQ-1) and explicitly said 'REVIEWER should confirm this reading... before ELIXIR-DEV builds it' -- i.e. this gap was flagged, not caught in review, and never revisited when the tests were written.

WHY EXISTING TESTS DIDN'T CATCH IT: EO-004/EO-005 pass reliably in isolation (12/12, per the issue record) and evidently pass most full-suite runs too, because the race window is narrow (the two start_rollout/resume_rollout calls inside one test run back-to-back in milliseconds) -- it only fires when another async test's tenant-activation commit lands inside that exact window, which needs real full-suite concurrency and is inherently non-deterministic.

REPRODUCTION ATTEMPT (real, not assumed): ran this test file concurrently, unpartitioned (single shared DB, so real races are possible, unlike the -N4 partitioned run which isolates DBs per partition), alongside 9 other TenantFixture-heavy files (tenant_provisioning_test.exs, column_promotion_test.exs, tenants_test.exs, tenant_solutions_test.exs, solution_pack_test.exs, service_catalog_test.exs, tenant_test.exs, instances_test.exs, entities_test.exs) for 3 iterations with randomized seeds. Actual outcome: 328 passed / 0 failed on iteration 1, 328/0 on iteration 2, 328/0 on iteration 3 (exit code 0 overall) -- the race was NOT reproduced live in this session. This is consistent with the mechanism (a narrow, non-deterministic timing window that depends on exactly which unrelated test's tenant-activation commit happens to land, i.e. depends on seed/scheduling) rather than evidence the mechanism doesn't exist -- the design doc's own OQ-1 independently confirms the vulnerable window is real, and the issue's own original report (RELEASE-VALIDATOR, ISS-0825) already observed the failure once live under -N4 full-suite load.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE: this is a TEST-file defect, not a production-code defect -- production's scope-refresh behavior in apply_to_existing_rollout/2 is the deliberately-chosen, explicitly-documented design (OQ-1), so the fix belongs in test/letflow/platform/migration_rollout_test.exs's EO-004 and EO-005 assertions, following the same pattern the adjacent 'queryable outcome record' test in the same file already uses: scope completion/count/already_current assertions to only the outcomes for the tenants each test itself created (e.g. filter Repo.aggregate/outcome-list checks by this test's own known tenant_ids or rollout_id-plus-tenant_id pairs) instead of asserting exact global row counts or `Enum.all?` over the full, shared-scope outcome/rollout set.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design. Justification: this is a real, traceable defect (confirmed by direct code trace of active_company_tenant_ids/0 and apply_to_existing_rollout/2, plus the design doc's own explicitly-flagged OQ-1 -- not speculation, and not merely CPU/host contention as originally suspected), with a concrete, scoped fix target (EO-004/EO-005's assertions in test/letflow/platform/migration_rollout_test.exs need the same tenant/rollout-scoped assertion pattern the adjacent 'queryable outcome record' test in the same file already uses). This is NOT the 'ORCH direct-action documentation close' route, because unlike ISS-0766/ISS-0868 (genuine environmental/infrastructure hazards with no fix target in the codebase) this issue has an identifiable, fixable test-code defect and an existing in-file precedent for the fix. It is NOT a 'no_defect' close either, since a mechanism was substantiated (design doc OQ-1 + code trace), even though a live race was not caught in this session's 3-iteration mixed-load reproduction attempt (328/328/328 passed, 0 failures) -- consistent with a narrow, non-deterministic timing window rather than absence of the defect.
